note: Page 1 of 3. Original spelling kept (“greatful,” “layed”). A repeated “and” is struck through in the original. If the letter dates from 1873, as P035 says, it speaks of both parents as living, which fits the 1874 death date for Phebe (P057).

entries.label: Page 1
entries.text:
My Dearly beloved daughter thy fathers and Mothers lives are just wearing out, and ere many months pass away, the Sun of their lives will have set; and thee will behold them no more on Earth in their material forms; and dear Child, knowing that I am poor in what is called worldly possessions & the probabilities are that I cannot bequeath to thee any property of that nature, I feel greatful that there is a wealth which I can and will cheerfully give to thee, that thee may use it daily during thy natural life and ~and~ be abundantly rewarded; and when thy sojourn on earth is ended, thee will receive thy great reward in the Summerland.

I enjoin it upon thee, Dear Child, to follow well the advice herein layed down, and thee cannot go much astray from the path of duty to thyself and to others.
